memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "Before I was afflicted I went astray, but now I keep Your word." — Psalm 119:67

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
The legendary Vance Havner once drew a profound parallel between a servant of God and a bottle of syrup. On the label of the medicine or the syrup, we often find the instruction: "Shake well before use." Why the shaking? Because over time, the potent ingredients the very essence that provides flavor or healing settle at the bottom. In our spiritual lives, we often suffer from a "sediment" of lethargy, pride, and complacency. We settle into our comforts, and our spiritual vitality sinks to the base of our souls.
God, in His infinite wisdom, knows that a world dying from the "cancer" of sin cannot be cured by a stagnant witness. He needs the heavenly medicine to be potent and well-mixed. Therefore, He allows the "shaking." He permits trials, shifts our circumstances, and stirs our spirits. It isn’t to destroy us, but to redistribute His grace and power throughout our entire being. To be "shaken well" by God is to be prepared for maximum impact. If you feel your world is shaking today, remember: the Great Physician is simply preparing the medicine for a world in need.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "God uses broken things. It takes broken soil to produce a crop, broken clouds to give rain, broken grain to give bread, broken alabaster to give forth perfume." — Vance Havner

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, I thank You that You care enough about my service to stir my soul. Forgive my lethargy and the way I settle into my own comforts. If You are shaking my life today, let it result in a perfect mixture of Your grace, love, and power. Make me a potent medicine for a dying world. Use me for Your glory. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Don't be afraid of the "shaking" seasons. When things feel unsettled, it’s a sign that God is about to pour you out into someone else's life. You are the medicine this world needs, and God is just making sure you're at your best before He uses you.
